pr_body:
When a passenger is trying to enter a transport, it will move next to the transport. When it moves adjacent the transport becomes reserved and stops moving. The passenger can then enter it.

For a fast moving transport, it may be moving fast enough than when stopped it has managed to get out of range of the target. Currently the activity then cancels without completing the enter as the passenger is no longer next to the transport. We can detect when this occurs and re-approach the target - allowing the enter to succeed rather than cancelling.

Fixes #19382
pr_comments:
Nice spot, I had the conditionals messed up a bit. If it had tried a second approach it would unconditionally enter. In the fixed version it only enters if it's in the right position.

With the fixed version applied to your replay, the activity now cancels because it was unable to enter after two attempts (this causes a desync in the replay, obviously).

I think it fails even two attempts because the jeep is still stopping, but it swings around the infantry over several cells, so it's adjacent to the infatry for quite a bit and thus triggers several "approach complete - try and enter" steps.

Maybe that's a case to try 3 approaches? Or maybe we just accept the hack will help but not fix everything. An alternative approach would be to fix the root causde, this is to say when `TryStartEnter` returns true because the enter is ready to start, it has actually stopped the transport in an adjacent cell such that it can actually be entered successfully.
Fair enough. Hopefully another PR can find a robust solution to the problem.

review_comments: I think it's not a good to assume that the transport will stop. A single pass flag does not seem correct

Indeed, we're limited by what dervied classes will do here when `TryStartEnter` is called. The `RideTransport` activity will reserve the transport, which will lock it in place. But other derived classes do not do such an action when `TryStartEnter` is called. Though to be fair some of them are operating on targets that are usually immobile, e.g. buildings.

I ruled out retrying forever here, as it is possible to recreate the original bug with naval transports, e.g. as below:
![image](https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/assets/3399086/1651c5a2-eb07-4e36-967f-c6b3786d5d38)

If you end up in this scenario, retrying forever is a big problem. The transport is locked in place and won't respond to commands as it is reserved. But the infantry cannot path to the transport - as that would require it being able to step into the water. So these units would be stuck in place if we did an endless retry. In this situation the current behaviour of cancelling the activity seems better than deadlocking the units.

So if one attempt can sometimes fail, and we don't want to restart forever, the next natural step was to try twice, which seems sufficient to fix the original bug, whilst still allowing the activity to cancel itself if the 2nd attempt fails. I figure that is useful for both the navel transport issue - where it will otherwise be stuck forever, but also useful for some weird edge case where you somehow keep getting next to the enter target, yet it has always moved by the time you try and enter it.

So I think the two attempt strategy actually makes a lot of sense here. For the `RideTransport` case when the target will be locked from moving, it neatly fixes the needing to take an extra step to complete the enter scenario. For other classes it may not be a guarentee. But limiting the retry count to 2 prevents any badness, whilst still possibly improving the number of times it will work. If the first path got you close but then something fudged it at the last moment, having a second go knowing the target is likely still close seems like a decent thing to try.

Anyway that was a long braindump of how I got to this policy as a solution - but I'm open to other options if you can think of one.

Hmm, so the issue is that `RideTransport` assumes that if it returns true in TryStartEnter that it will either successfully enter or be cancelled. That seems a bit wrong the the unit is locked up even during the cancellation process

I think the double retry approach is more a hack than a proper solution, and should be labelled as such
